A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same stick-breaking attention study despite the revised title. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, including the retained RULER appendix and v2's additional material.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic recall experiments, language-model evaluations, length-extrapolation results, RULER evaluations and implementation throughput measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds component ablations, mixture-of-experts model evaluations and context-extension experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the two-phase backward procedure and quadratic intermediate storage with a backward pass using atomic gradient additions and linear memory. Appendix C also introduces head-wise Group Norm and explicitly formulates the learned remainder-bias variant; v1 had already mentioned remainder experiments. The core attention-weight formula remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Table 5 adds MATH evaluation alongside the existing mathematical and general-language tasks. Figure 8 adds predictive-likelihood evaluation on Pile 10k, which v1 used for runtime measurement. The original synthetic recall, Wikitext, downstream NLP and RULER coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding main experiments retain their comparator sets, including ALiBi, FIRE, NoPE, RoPE, sliding-window attention and the public language models. TinyLlama already appears in v1's Table 3. Appendix C reuses softmax comparisons; the explicit FA2 name in v2 does not establish replacement of a different throughput baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds dense-model ablation and 6.5B/28.6B MoE settings, reporting training budgets of 1.25T, 2T and 3T tokens. Its context-extension experiment introduces 6,250 continuation steps at 16K context, a specified learning-rate schedule, a 4M-token batch and RoPE scaling factor 4. These are additional protocols, not established revisions to the retained main experiments.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds quantitative comparisons of stick-breaking without modifications, with remainder bias, and with remainder bias plus Group Norm. Figure 8 adds a controlled analysis of whether continued long-context training improves subsequent extrapolation. V1 contains neither this component table nor the continuation-training analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and curves without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional appendix results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds Table 5 and Figure 8 results, including average scores of 60.4 versus 58.6 for the 6.5B stick-breaking and softmax models. Reported throughput changes from 16.27 versus 19.5 to 21 versus 29.5 billion tokens/day alongside the implementation revision, and Figure 5 updates plotted likelihood values. Tables 2–4 and the RULER results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the recency-ordering condition and its equal-logit assumption, repairing the stated mathematical property. Figure 1 also corrects formula indexing. New Appendix A expands the derivation of the already-present log-space identity rather than introducing a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract reframes the contribution from proposing an alternative attention mechanism to investigating it at larger scale. The conclusion adds initial evidence for stick-breaking-specific Transformer modifications. The central claims about positional-embedding-free attention, length extrapolation and competitive downstream performance remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting remainder bias to attention sinks and Group Norm to varying output norms, and interprets the new continuation experiment as evidence for better context extension. It also extends the few-shot interpretation to in-context learning and removes v1's qualification that public-model comparisons may depend on data mixtures or training hyperparameters.

D1.justification: V2 supplies revised kernel pseudocode and memory-access details, newly mentions PTX softplus computation, and documents MoE expert configurations and context-extension hyperparameters. These substantially expand implementation and reproduction information. The repository link and existing hardware disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to TinyLlama and Differential Transformer, using the latter to contextualize head-wise normalization. Its title and abstract emphasize scaling and implementation more explicitly, while the existing positioning relative to geometric attention and earlier stick-breaking work largely remains.

P1.justification: The title, author order and publication header change, with localized rewrites of the abstract, implementation discussion and experimental interpretation. New appendices expand the document, but the main section sequence and most existing prose are retained. V2 introduces unresolved references such as 'Appendix ??' and 'In Figure ,'.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to explain atomic accumulation, and the two backward pseudocode displays are replaced by one. V2 adds Table 5 and Figure 8, revises Figure 5's scales and legend presentation, and relocates several existing displays. The RULER appendix figure is retained under Appendix B rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The revised linear-memory procedure directly addresses v1's quadratic-memory scaling limitation. Appendix C substantially strengthens the practical assessment through quantified component comparisons, larger MoE experiments and controlled context-extension training. These gains outweigh presentation defects and interpretive limitations: cross-references remain broken, and adding Group Norm leaves the dense-model average unchanged at the reported precision. The improvement rests on the implementation advance and more informative evidence, not on changes to the retained benchmark tables.
